author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, Terri-Ann Richards explores why so many capable young people stop themselves before they try. She introduces the idea of the belief gap, the invisible space between potential and action, and reveals how belief, not ability, often determines who applies, who speaks up, and who steps forward.

Drawing on psychology, mental health research, and lived experience, this talk examines how belief shapes confidence, participation, and long-term outcomes. It challenges the assumption that motivation or talent is the problem, and instead shows how quiet self-doubt, avoidance, and learned hesitation can stall potential before failure ever occurs. This talk is for students, educators, parents, leaders, and anyone who has ever talked themselves out of an opportunity they were capable of pursuing.

#TEDx #Belief #Youth #Potential

title: How to help young people take more risks | Terri-Ann Richards | TEDxUNB

author: TEDx Talks
description: We’ve all been there: you pick up your phone to check the time and wake up thirty minutes later, buried in a scroll-induced trance. Tim Evers, a Music teacher at Schule Schloss Salem, deconstructs the stages of the "Rabbit Hole", applying the famous Marshmallow Experiment to our digital lives. By analyzing the stages of distraction from the perspective of a fellow user—not a lecturer—he proposes a radical solution: the power of sitting in silence to unlock the creativity and initiative that the "Algorithm" tries to steal. Tim Evers is a music teacher, house tutor, and orchestra conductor at Salem International College. When he isn't directing ensembles or mentoring students, he is a keen observer of how technology reshapes the human brain. As an educator and a smartphone user himself, he is passionate about finding "analog" pockets of silence in an increasingly loud digital world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a loca
title: Going down the rabbit hole | Tim Evers | TEDxSchule Schloss Salem

author: TEDx Talks
description: Catherine’s speech dives into the complexity of our food system in relation to the climate crisis, including production, commercialized farming, and unsustainable methods. Through her work as a paleontologist, Catherine has learned to identify eras of extinction, and recognizes that our food system is putting us on the edge of another. Not only does Catherine identify the food system as a large cause of the climate crisis, she also offers actionable solutions to both policymakers and consumers. Catherine Badgley, a professor in the University of Michigan Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, demonstrates to us the grave state that our climate is in, and then offers hope for a way forward. I am a professor in the Residential College and the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology [in LSA if important]. I study the response of terrestrial ecosystems to environmental changes over Earth's history and the environmental impacts of the global food system. I live on a farm, w
title: Achieving a radiant food system | Catherine Badgley | TEDxUofM

author: TEDx Talks
description: Leadership is often treated as a rare gift, but what if it was a built-in propensity? Drawing on the educational laws of Kurt Hahn and the "Salem" philosophy, Tim von Lackum explores how specific environments can cultivate a natural urge to take initiative. Through stories of youth climate activists and his own experiences in a specialized learning community, Tim explores why the next generation isn't just waiting for their turn to lead—they are already doing it. A Year 1 IB student at Salem International College, Tim von Lackum is immersed in an educational system designed to foster character and leadership. He is fascinated by the intersection of institutional history and modern activism, focusing on how the principles of his schooling apply to global movements like climate justice. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How Kurt Hahn's Laws Inspire Leadership | Tim von Lackum | TEDxSchule Schloss Salem

author: TEDx Talks
description: "With great power comes great responsibility" is more than a movie quote—it is a call to action for the modern era. Antonia Werner explores the uncomfortable tension of being "privileged" in a world of crisis. Moving past the paralysis of guilt, she argues that those with the most resources have the highest obligation to lead. Inspired by the courage of those who fight with nothing, Antonia offers a roadmap for using our advantages to amplify the voices that need it most. Antonia Werner is a Year 2 IB student at Salem International College with a deep interest in social justice and international relations. After being moved by stories of refugees and activists who risk everything for basic rights, she has focused her work on how students in elite educational environments can pivot from passive "privilege" to active global citizenship. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/
title: With great privilege comes great responsibility | Antonia Werner | TEDxSchule Schloss Salem

author: TEDx Talks
description: We are taught to fear what we cannot predict, especially in a world defined by global conflict and environmental instability. But what if uncertainty isn't a threat to be managed, but a lens to be used? Amelia Obermayer challenges the traditional educational focus on "right answers," suggesting instead that our greatest strength lies in our ability to remain present and adaptable when the path forward is foggy. Currently completing her final year of the IB diploma program at Salem International College, Amelia Obermayer stands at the threshold of an uncertain future—and she too is slightly afraid of it. Driven by the pressures of a changing global landscape, she explores the intersection of education and adaptability, seeking to redefine how her generation views the "unknown." This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Graduating into the Unknown | Amelia Obermayer | TEDxSchule Schloss Salem

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world obsessed with "useful" degrees and high-ROI careers, is there still room for the philosopher? Julia Kupchik argues that philosophy hasn't become useless, it has become invisible. Using everything from Batman’s moral code to the way we question our daily choices, Julia illustrates that philosophy isn't just for dusty libraries—it is the essential tool we use every time we decide what is "right" versus what is "efficient." Julia Kupchik is a Year 1 IB student at Salem International College with a strong curiosity for the "why" behind the "what." Despite the modern push toward purely utilitarian career paths, Julia remains a staunch advocate for the classical humanities, believing that a world without philosophy is a world without a moral compass. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Has philosophy become useless? | Julia Kupchik | TEDxSchule Schloss Salem

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDx Regeneron talk, April shares her journey from clinical practice to biotech and explores how social determinants of health shape vision and health outcomes. She underscores the power of cross-sector collaboration to address challenges that medicine alone cannot solve and calls for collective action to build a more equitable future. April McCullough, M.D., is an ophthalmologist and Senior Medical Director in Global Development at Regeneron whose career is driven by a passion to advance sight-saving care and health equity for patients. Her work bridges clinical practice, industry, and community impact.

April earned a BA in Biological Sciences from Cornell University and an MD from NYU School of Medicine, then completed her ophthalmology residency at New York Medical College. She began clinical practice in the New York City metropolitan area, treating a diverse population including the underserved, where patient stories sharpened her resolve to improve outcomes beyond the exa
title: Hidden factors determine who gets to see | April McCullough | TEDxRegeneron

author: TEDx Talks
description: What would happen if we all chose to live our lives authentically? Although it is easy to say, it is difficult to put into practice - but it is exactly what our world needs right now.  Meher Parsinni is a Senior in High School planning to pursue Film as a career in the future. In addition to public speaking and filming, Meher spends her time leading numerous organizations at her school: The STEP Team, South Asian Student Union, Philosophy & Film Club, and the student newspaper. Her heritage plays a crucial role in shaping her identity, storytelling, and advocacy, as she uses her voice to speak out against disparities in our world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
Dünya büyük bir tiyatro sahnesiyse, biz gerçekten kendi rolümüzü mü oynuyoruz?
​Oyuncu Meltem Pamirtan, Shakespeare’den Marcuse’a uzanan bir yolculukla; büyümenin getirdiği 'yabancılaşmayı' ve modern dünyada kaybolan hissetme yetimizi sorguluyor. Değişime uyum sağlamanın hayatta kalmak için tek yol olduğunu hatırlatan Pamirtan, maskelerin ardındaki 'gerçek seni' bulmanın ve sahnede yeniden var olmanın yollarını anlatıyor. Sahne üzerinde olduğu kadar yaşamın içinde de bir keşif yolcusu olan Meltem Pamirtan; küçük yaşta dans, müzik ve ritimle tanışarak duyguların dilini öğrenmiş, merakıyla sanatı ve insanı anlamaya adamış bir oyuncudur. Hayatı beş duyuyla hisseden ve her karakterde hem kendini hem de insanlığı arayan Pamirtan için oyunculuk, varoluşun en derin halini anlamanın bir yoludur. Sahnede öğrenmeye devam eden bir ruhla, insanın özündeki hikayeyi keşfetmeye devam ediyor. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local co

description: Marmara Denizi’ni yüzerek geçen ilk Türk kadın sporcu olmak sadece fiziksel bir güç değil, çelik gibi bir irade gerektirir. Milli yüzücü ve mühendis Hilal Zeyneb Saraç, 22 yıllık spor kariyerindeki rekorların ardında yatan görünmez zorlukları ve her düştüğünde ayağa kalkmasını sağlayan o motivasyonu paylaşıyor. Açık suların belirsizliğinden savunma sanayiinin disiplinine uzanan bu yolculukta, sınırların sadece zihnimizde olduğunu keşfedeceksiniz. 22 yılını spora adamış, rekorlarla dolu bir kariyerin sahibi olan Hilal Zeyneb Saraç, Marmara Denizi’ni yüzerek geçen ilk Türk kadın sporcu ünvanına sahiptir. Sporcu kimliğinin yanı sıra Havacılık ve Uzay alanındaki mühendislik çalışmalarıyla savunma sanayiinde de adından söz ettiren Saraç; fiziksel dayanıklılığı zihinsel disiplinle birleştirerek imkansız görüne

She shares how she first stepped into the industry, the learning curves that followed, and the reality behind the glamour. From facing body shaming and constant judgment to building confidence in a competitive space, Arunima reflects on the resilience it took to keep going. She also opens up about balancing her engineering career alongside modeling, redefining what it means to pursue multiple ambitions. Her story offers an honest look at the industry while celebrating growth, self-belief, and the courage to claim one’s space. For Arunima Jayan, the path from writing code to claiming the crown of Miss Kerala 2025 was not a change of direction, but a masterclass in versatility. author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this insightful TEDx talk, Mohit Sharma shares his transformative experience of living in one of the most extreme environments on Earth. Having spent nearly two years in Antarctica as part of scientific expeditions, he set out believing that the journey would test his strength, endurance and resilience. However, what he discovered there was far more profound.

In Antarctica, there are no safety nets. Through his experiences, Mohit realised that the environment he stepped into is a test of true responsibility and strength. A simple moment of awareness, choosing to act instead of ignore, can make all the difference.

He reflects on how responsibility reveals itself in quiet yet powerful ways. It appears in taking initiative before being asked, in showing up even when it is inconvenient, and in acting on what feels slightly wrong before it becomes a visible problem. These actions create stability, trust and collective success.

Through real-life moments and introspection, Mohit highli
title: The Art of Not Looking Away: Lessons from My Journey in Antarctica | Mohit Sharma | TEDxJMC

description:
In this evocative TEDx talk, Kriti Singhal reflects on a deeply personal journey marked by responsibility, self-doubt, and eventual self-realisation. As a self-described “quintessential eldest daughter,” she recounts the weight of expectations that shaped her early years. Her experiences reveal the daily tryst between duty and identity, especially within environments that prioritise achievement over self-exploration.

It was during her undergraduate years that this narrative began to shift. As she threw herself into a range of pursuits, spanning theatre, dance and editorial work, what seemed, at first, like a scattered exploration slowly began to take shape. In the midst of it all, a quiet pattern surfaced, drawing her towards a natural inclination for leadership.

This inclination found  expression in the founding of her first venture, The Education Tree, where her instincts translated into real impact. During this experience, she encountered a version of herself that had previously
title: In the Process of Becoming | Kriti Singhal | TEDxJMC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Kairavi Bharat Ram introduces her mantra for life - Pivot, framing it as a conscious recognition that one can redirect their path at any moment. Drawing from her experiences in the business world, she highlights how this capacity to realign oneself becomes essential in navigating an ever-evolving landscape, where growth is not a mere reaction but constant adaptation and realignment. 

Extending beyond professional insights, Kairavi turns inward to reflect on her personal encounters with depression, anxiety, and self-doubt. She talks about the illusion of permanence, reflecting on the drastic comparison of who she was then and who she is now. From the quiet corners of her room to building a nationwide beauty brand, she adopts the lesson of impermanence into her personal and professional life. 

As a founder, she further interrogates the double standards we set for ourselves, forgetting objectivity when things become personal and choosing to blame on
title: The Myth of Permanence  | Kairavi Bharat Ram | TEDxJMC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this incisive TEDx talk, Dr. Kiran Sethi shares her deeply personal journey of transformation, confronted with a powerful realization that reclaiming her health is not merely a personal choice, but a profound social duty that extends far beyond herself. 

Dr. Sethi vividly illustrates that being healthy is not a private luxury; it is a necessity and a shared responsibility. When she met with illness in her own life, she made a conscious shift towards healthier living, committing herself to sustained and intentional change. In just six months, her dedication to better habits reshaped her own life where her decision for a healthier lifestyle translated into real impact within her family. 

She posits that our choices reverberate across multiple layers of social connection, shaping not only those within our immediate circle but also extending their influence across generations, with the capacity to disrupt entrenched cycles of poor health. Through her formulation of the “3 by 3 health
title: The Contagious Power of One Healthy Choice  | Dr. Kiran Sethi | TEDxJMC

author: TEDx Talks
description: When the version of success you once relied on stops working, failure can feel less like a setback and more like losing a part of yourself. This talk stays with that uncomfortable in-between - where nothing feels certain, and moving forward no longer looks the way it used to. Drawing from her own experience, Thuc Anh reflects on this redirection and introduces the Phoenix Principle as a way of understanding transformation, not as a dramatic comeback, but as a slow process of becoming. Because sometimes, the fire never truly goes out - it simply burns in places no one is looking. Van Luong Thuc Anh is a Grade 12 English-specialized student at Le Thanh Tong High School for the Gifted, once known for a record of academic excellence that seemed almost predictable. For years, she believed that effort would always translate into achievement, and that success was something you could secure if you worked hard enough. That belief began to unravel when failure disrupted the path she had always
title: When the Fire Stops Winning | Anh Van Luong Thuc | TEDxGreenwichUniversityDanang

author: TEDx Talks
description: Imagine a single word acting as a match that burns down your most precious relationship in just a few seconds. For many young people, the "gasoline" of academic pressure, the "wind" of adolescent impulsivity and the "hidden embers" of past trauma make these emotional explosions feel unavoidable. Dinh Van Thanh Khoi explores how we can stop reacting impulsively and instead transform our internal wildfire into a guiding torch of calmness. By mastering simple techniques like mindful pausing and root-cause reflection, he demonstrates how anyone can become the "boss" of their emotions. This talk serves as a roadmap to help you stop wasting time on regrets and start living a life that is full and happy. Dinh Van Thanh Khoi is a third-year student at Greenwich Viet Nam, Danang campus, who turned a devastating personal loss into a mission for emotional mastery. After watching his own uncontrolled anger burn down a meaningful relationship, Khoi dedicated himself to understanding why the "flame
title: Torch or Ashes: the Choice is Yours | Khoi Dinh Van Thanh | TEDxGreenwichUniversityDanang

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the most important question in life is not “What job should I choose?” but “Where is the fun part?”. In this talk, Phương Nam reflects on how he chased joy into stand-up comedy, only to discover that even a job built on laughter can become heavy with pressure and responsibility. Through stories of burnout, creative struggle and self-discovery, he shows that joy does not always disappear when life gets hard.  Sometimes, it simply changes its form. In the end, this talk is a reminder that while life may be full of challenges, we can still choose to walk through it with humor, honesty and joy. Lê Nguyên Khang is a Business Administration student at Greenwich Viet Nam, Da Nang Campus who carries two burning flames within him: the desire to become his family’s pride, and an intense passion for rap. He was once seen as a “golden child” in the eyes of many, until he became completely consumed by the silence of his own failures. He has long struggled with the question of how to return
title: Where is the fun part? | Nam Tran Phuong | TEDxGreenwichUniversityDanang

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the problem is not that you are not working hard enough, but that your effort has no clear direction? In todays fast paced and highly visible world, it is easy to confuse constant movement with meaningful progress. In this talk, Le Minh Quan shares his personal experience of doing everything "right" yet feeling lost inside, revealing how comparison and external expectations can quietly drain our inner fire. Through three transformative shifts: Pause, Choose, and Commit, he offers a new way of thinking about effort, one that is guided by intention rather than pressure. Because in the end, true direction is not something we find outside, but something we build from within. Le Minh Quan is a Business Management student at the University of Greenwich, Da Nang. Once driven by the belief that constant hard work would naturally lead to clarity and success, he found himself lost despite doing everything “right.” Through a period of confusion and silent pressure, Quan began to question
title: From Reaction to Direction | Quan Le Minh | TEDxGreenwichUniversityDanang

author: TEDx Talks
description: Have you ever achieved a major milestone, only to feel a terrifying, isolating fear that you’re secretly a fraud waiting to be exposed? That paralyzing feeling has a scientific name: Imposter Syndrome. But how do you beat a mental trap that makes smart people feel so incompetent? The answer lies in decoding a famous psychological graph: the Dunning-Kruger Effect. In this talk, a young founder shares her lonely journey of watching her startups hit zero profit, plunging her straight into the notorious 'Valley of Despair.' By breaking down the psychology behind self-doubt, she proves that feeling like a fake isn't a glitch in your brain—it's just the invisible 'tax' you pay for leveling up. Watch to discover how to use this psychological graph to forge your way out of the dark! Khanh Bang is a 17-year-old high school student, English tutor, and the ambitious founder behind two start-up business, Selythephoto and Selythehandmade. Although she was once the classic 'gifted kid' living on he
title: How to make Imposter Syndrome work for you | Bang Le Nguyen Khanh | TEDxGreenwichUniversityDanang

description: An emotional ride for a Hispanic kid who had a passion to be great at everything, but words and the disconnection of culture restricted a world I couldn’t express. Growing up in a Hispanic household, not speaking a vital part of my culture crushed my heart. author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk is about the quiet ways creativity gets shut down.

Not by rules or laws, but by fear, doubt, and the need to be perfect. It starts when you are young. You stop raising your hand. You stop sharing weird ideas. You start playing safe.

These are the real crimes against creativity.

This talk calls them out. It shows how we learn to silence ourselves and how we can take that voice back. Because creativity is not rare. It is something most people just stopped using. Unyime is a 16-year-old high school student named Unyimeabasi Etop has a deep love for technology and science. She intends to study software engineering in college because she is curious about how systems work and how rational concepts are turned into useful tools. She selects science because it pushes her to think critically, spot trends, and find precise solutions to challenging issues. title: Crimes against Creativity | Uyime Etop | TEDxStart Rite Schools Abuja

description: In her TEDxEnsley Avenue ED talk, “Stop Praising Grit: No One Makes It Alone”, Montiqua Mathers-Pettway challenges the widely accepted belief that grit is the ultimate indicator of success. She reveals that when we celebrate the resilience of young people who “make it out,” we overlook the systems and adults responsible for providing support. Rather than being a strength alone, grit is often a response to environments where critical needs were not met. Her talk challenges the idea that resilience alone drives success and calls leaders, educators, and communities to take greater responsibility. Are we applauding survival when what is truly required is a commitment to stand in the gap? Montiqua Mathers-Pettway is a leadership and workplace culture expert with more than two decades of Human Resources experience. title: Stop Praising Grit: No One Makes It Alone | Montiqua Mathers-Pettway, MS | TEDxEnsley Avenue ED

description:
The speaker discusses AI’s growing presence in everyday life and the need to use it ethically. He warns that publishing AI-generated news without careful scrutiny can cause misinterpretation and panic. Newsrooms’ heavy reliance on AI, he argues, threatens the creativity and critical thinking that are central to journalism. Munir S. Mohammed is a journalist, writer, and researcher based in Ethiopia. With hundreds of articles published in the country’s leading outlets, he has built a reputation for curiosity, rigor, and a data-driven approach to storytelling. Trained in economics, Munir brings analytical depth to his work, blending insight with narrative clarity.
An autodidact across multiple fields, he has also produced compelling personal stories on mental health, women’s rights, and labor issues. title: Preserving Human Intelligence in an AI World | Munir Shemsu Mohammed | TEDxICS Addis Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, the speaker recounts his journey to becoming a filmmaker. He highlights core values—empathy, passion, hope, fear , and curiosity—as essential qualities for the story telling through film as a craft. He also speaks about cultivating a habit of reading widely across genres and discovering stories everywhere. Based in the vibrant city of Mumbai, Srikanth Velagaleti is a seasoned filmmaker and storyteller with 15 years of experience in the Indian film industry. His directorial debut, Utt Pataang, garnered critical acclaim and showcased his talent alongside notable actors. Passionate about philosophy, the environment, and animal welfare, he is set to release Dinchak Dinchak, a socially relevant film addressing the crucial topic of sex education for youth, reflecting his commitment to illuminating untold stories. With a dedication to pushing artistic boundaries, Srikanth continues to inspire through his diverse projects and lectures on filmmaking. This talk was given at a TEDx
title: Highs Lows and Buffaloes | Srikanth Velagaleti | TEDxICS Addis Youth
